extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical investigators (assistant professors) and institutional research administrators/nominators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and institutional limited-submission rules for nominating and applying to the 2026 Pew Biomedical Scholars program, including eligibility, required materials, selection priorities, and budgetary restrictions. Intended for assistant professors running independent labs and offices managing the single institutional nomination slot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctorate requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a doctorate in biomedical sciences, medicine, or a related field, including engineering or the physical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment rank and independent lab requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As of Sept. 3, 2025, run an independent lab and hold a full-time appointment at the rank of assistant professor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments such as research assistant professor, adjunct assistant professor, assistant professor research track, visiting professor, or instructor are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-year assistant professor eligibility window (appointment date limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must not have been appointed as an assistant professor and run an independent lab at any institution prior to June 11, 2021, whether or not such an appointment was on a tenure track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent in clinical internships, residencies, in work toward board certification, or on parental leave does not count as part of this four-year limit. Candidates who need an exception on the four-year limit should contact Pew’s program office so reviewers are aware an exception has been given. Note: eligibility criteria have been temporarily expanded to account for COVID-related lab shutdowns; this extension ends after this application cycle and the window will revert to three years for 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application attempt and nomination restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: May apply to the program a maximum of two times. All applicants must be nominated by their institution and must complete the 2026 online application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants have appointments at more than one eligible nominating institution or affiliate, they may not reapply in a subsequent year from a different nominating entity. May not be nominated for the Pew Scholars Program and the Pew-Stewart Scholars Program for Cancer Research in the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope exclusion — no clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: This program does not fund clinical trials research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research quality expectations — creativity, high impact, interdisciplinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong proposals will incorporate particularly creative and pioneering approaches to basic, translational, and applied biomedical research. Candidates whose work is based on biomedical principles but who bring in concepts and theories from more diverse fields are encouraged to apply. Ideas with the potential to produce an unusually high impact are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — project, researcher, and past accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the successful candidates will be based on a detailed description of the work that the applicant proposes to undertake, evaluations of the candidate’s performance, and notable past accomplishments, including honors, awards, and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating the candidates, the National Advisory Committee gives considerable weight to both the project proposal and the researcher, including evidence that the candidate is a successful independent investigator and has the skill set needed to carry out their high-impact proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator effort expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that Pew scholars will spend at least 80 percent of their time in work or activities related to the accomplishment of their overall research goals (which are not restricted to the specific aims proposed for this award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew provides flexible support to the general research aims of the scholar and does not require effort reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional limited-submission process — portal and template requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs must submit their application as a Limited Submission through the Research Initiatives and Infrastructure (RII) Application Portal and use the provided template (RII-Limited-Submission-Application-Template).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Page Proposal Summary formatting and page-limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-Page Proposal Summary (1.0” margins; single-spaced; font type: Arial, Helvetica, or Georgia typeface; font size: 11 pt). Page limit includes references and illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages that exceed the 2-page limit will be excluded from review. You must use the template linked above.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: CV – (5 pages maximum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal-required personal/administrative data
rubrics_metrics.description: The portal requires information about the PIs in addition to department and contact information, including the 10-digit USC ID#, Gender, and Ethnicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please have this material prepared before beginning this application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: An award of $75,000 per year for four years will be provided to the sponsoring institution for use by the scholar, subject to annual review of the scholar’s progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant agreements will be issued in August of the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The awarded funds may be used at the discretion of the Pew scholar, for personnel, equipment, supplies, or travel directly related to the scholar’s research and as to best advance his or her research and career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator salary cap
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the award that may be used for the principal investigator’s salary is limited to $12,500 per year (including benefits) or $50,000 over the duration of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student and postdoctoral salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no limits on student or postdoctoral salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & administration (indirect cost) limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Not more than 8 percent ($24,000) of the total award value may be allocated for facilities and administration (F&A) charges or indirect costs (IDCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover and no-cost extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the funds not be immediately required, they may be accumulated and carried over through the grant period and, with written approval of the program office, the grant may receive a no-cost extension for one additional year (without additional funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Subawards are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination slot and internal deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Slots: 1 (institutional limited-submission slot). Internal Deadline: Friday, March 28th, 2025, 5pm PT (Closed). LOI: May 14, 2025 – nomination form. External Deadline: September 3, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must follow internal limited-submission processes to select and nominate their single candidate; missing internal deadlines will prevent nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict with other funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding from the NIH, other government sources, and project grants from nonprofit associations do not pose a conflict with the Pew scholars program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions concerning eligibility, contact Pew Biomedical Programs (scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org) in advance of applying.
